record.context_brief: Graphs embeddable in the torus but not the Klein bottle.
record.original_question: A graph is called orientably simple if it embeds in the torus T but does not embed in the Klein bottle K. Characterize the orientably simple graphs, without requiring the characterization to be by excluded minors.

evidence.quote: A graph G that embeds in T but not K we call orientably simple. The problem is to characterize orientably simple graphs, not necessarily by excluded minors.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T denote the torus (the closed orientable surface of genus 1) and let K denote the Klein bottle (the closed non-orientable surface of genus 2). A finite graph G is said to be orientably simple if G admits a topological embedding into T but does not admit any topological embedding into K.

Give a characterization of the class of orientably simple graphs. The characterization is not required to be in terms of forbidden (excluded) minors; any structural, combinatorial, or topological description that determines exactly which graphs are orientably simple is acceptable.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive characterization of graphs that embed in the torus but not in the Klein bottle. Related literature addresses graphs triangulating both surfaces, 6-regular Klein bottle graphs, and spanning planar subgraphs, but no general characterization of "orientably simple" graphs was found. The status appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Constructing the Graphs That Triangulate Both the Torus and the Klein Bottle
status_evidence.snippet: All the graphs that can be embedded on both the torus and the Klein bottle as their triangulations can be constructed.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses graphs embeddable on both surfaces, but does not provide a general characterization of those embeddable in T but not K.

status_evidence.title: Minor-minimal 6-regular graphs in the Klein bottle
status_evidence.snippet: No 6-regular graph admits an embedding in both the torus and the Klein bottle.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural results are known for restricted classes (e.g., 6-regular graphs), but a full characterization of orientably simple graphs is not given.
